title: The lines hpcworker prints for a program to read
description: Each family is a line protocol: a line is matched whole, after the reader strips terminal codes, drops a carriage return and trims; a glued keepalive is removed before matching (docs/V11_CONTRACT.md sections 5.3 to 5.5, 9, 11 and 8.3; docs/V12_CONTRACT.md 'The key' and 'The gate'). Patterns use only what JavaScript and Python regular expressions share. A line that matches none of a family's patterns is text for a person, never an event. vectors/ holds what the real writer printed.

step.written_by: hpcworker connect, and the gate's connect

lines.note: "-" for a field Claude Code did not give

rules: each step line at most once, in this order
the exit status is 0 after done, else the failure code's

login.written_by: the sign-in sitting (connect's, and `hpcworker claude login --plain`)

lines.pattern: ^HPCW-LOGIN: on (\S+); checking whether you are signed in already$
^HPCW-LOGIN: starting Claude Code's sign-in; waiting for the sign-in link$
^HPCW-LOGIN: (a menu appeared; chose the first entry|the menu is still up; pressed Enter again)$

lines.note: opened only when it is a Claude subscription's sign-in page on claude.ai or claude.com over https, never platform.claude.com

lines.pattern: ^HPCW-LOGIN: paste the code from that page$
^HPCW-LOGIN: that code was not accepted; paste it again$

lines.note: at least every 20 s from HPCW-STEP signin; remove it wherever it appears inside a line
any other progress line: words for a person

progress.written_by: worker start, the job and worker status, one line per event in <state_dir>/<name>/progress.log

sentences.text: Asked the grid for a computer
Stopped: waiting for your Claude sign-in timed out

rules: the longest sentence that matches wins
a sentence with an argument is followed by ": " and the argument
any other line is for Details only

gate.written_by: hpcworker gate, the forced command of the browser key's line
gate.stream: stdout, but missing, not-plain and too-large on stderr

lines.note: due: the day the browser key's oldest line expires (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC), never when the site sets no expiry, - when it does and no line of ours is there

rules: read a gate line by its prefix (HPCW- or {"v":1): a ~/.bashrc may print first

key.written_by: hpcworker browser-key and the gate's forget

login-setup.written_by: hpcworker login-setup, typed by the student
rules: the last non-empty line says how it ended; only done is success

lines.pattern: ^Done\. The grid will not ask again\.$
